collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: An elder sits outside the hut in the evening, and a child asks whether they ever went away.

setup.name: The scene
setup.text: (subject) is sitting outside (subject.his/her) hut in the evening, watching the village go by. Over the years (subject.he/she) has seen people leave for a few days and come home tired, leave for a season and come home changed, and leave for good and send word, or not. (subject.He/she) has waved at a great many canoes. (subject.He/she) has said a great many goodbyes, some properly and some not. (subject.He/she) never went anywhere much (subject.him/her)self. (child), a child, stops in front of (subject.him/her) and asks, "Did you ever go away?" (subject) thinks about it. "Once," (subject.he/she) says, "for three days. I missed my own bed." (child) finds this hilarious and runs off to tell everyone. (subject) settles back, perfectly comfortable, to watch the sun go down from exactly where (subject.he/she) always watches it.
